comparison.objective: Candidate tunes and locks a shock absorber to control repeated carriage impacts; pr-1821 refits a long wardrobe rail by feeding one end into a closed support while tilted and swinging the other end into an open support.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate tests small-tool alignment, captive-set-screw operation, collar fine rotation, bounded tightening, and adjustment based on dynamic response. pr-1821 tests coordinated bimanual transport and reorientation of a long rigid part, tilt-in insertion, and seating into two spatially separated supports.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two consecutive non-bottoming, non-overloading stops with bounded stroke, rebound, and post-lock collar drift. pr-1821 requires both rail ends seated, the rail level within 1 degree, released at least 3 cm from both grippers, and still for 1 second. Both available spec versions state the same essential thresholds; neither includes dynamic tuning or setting retention.
comparison.reason: Although both involve bimanual coordination, the rail task evaluates long-part pose planning and dual-end seating, while the candidate evaluates tool-mediated adjustment and retained dynamic energy absorption.
